text: Done. Here

's where things landed.

**1. Trainer or DIY — hybrid.** The two probl
ems in your brief aren't the same kind of problem. The pulling is DIY: it's mechanical, and 5–10 foc
used minutes a day fixes it. The barking isn't, until one question is answered — fear-based and frustration-based reactivity look identical on the end
of a leash and need close to opposite protocols. Getting that call wrong costs you weeks of the
wrong homework. So: one paid hour to diagnose it, one cheap class for structure, and you do all the

reps. **$490 total.**

ages:**

ays daytime only — needs confirming |

I ruled out Off Leash K9 and Sit Means Sit despite heavy local
advertising — both e-collar-based, and AVSAB's 2021 statement is that aversives have no role in beha
viour modification, with no exception for reactivity or aggression. Worth knowing before someone recommends them to

you.

**3. Four weeks**, one subtask each with day-by-day drills and a written criterion for adv
ancing. Week 1 is deliberately trigger-free — you stop rehearsing the problem before you start rewi

ring it.

Two things I'd draw your attention to. First, the Wag'N'Train scheduling caveat is the one thing that could break the rec
ommendation, so ask about an evening slot in your first email rather than after paying; the fallback is already written up
as a subtask. Second, start the trigger journal in Week 1 even if you skip everything else — distance, what he did, recovery time, fear-

vs-frustration body language. It's the most useful thing you can hand a trainer, and it's free.
